data.title: seq storage lab: how .seq pages are stored

data.text:
Goal: the seq storage lab, reusable by every stage. It learns, by measuring, how .seq pages should be stored: plain text files with git, an append-only hash-chain log, or SQLite, on about 1,000 sample pages. Matthew: "What should be the design for the storage of it." (t451u). Lab band door: 90.50.10.0700.
Builder (pass 1): Codex (t439u; t453u). Checker: Claude, by hand: wf only refuses the builder as checker (src/cmd.rs:730).
Serves: no page yet. The pages that will use this lab are the storage pages of a later stage (roadmap stage 4, Safe storage). Each is listed here, and lists this lab back, when it is made.
Related lab: 90.50.10.0702 seq grammar lab (it describes what this lab stores).
Pass 1 done when: labs/0703/ is on returns with a throwaway Rust bench whose tests pass (cargo test --manifest-path labs/0703/Cargo.toml) and labs/0703/LAB-0703-SEQ-STORAGE.md with the options, the sample pages, a results table (write and read speed, size, hand-readability, tamper detection, write-once fit), one pick with reasons, and how to rerun; and the cross-check by Claude passes.

fields.overview: Builder: Codex (t439u). Checker: Claude, by hand (wf refuses only the builder as checker, src/cmd.rs:730). Why: t451u (docs/review/DIRECTOR-WORDS-t450-t453u.md:9) "What should be the design for the storage of it." This is a lab in the lab band (door 90.50.10.0700); it serves no page yet. The bench is throwaway: it lives only in labs/0703/, is its own crate (its Cargo.toml has an empty [workspace] table so it never joins the wf crate), and nothing in src/ or tests/ uses it. Sample shape, read only, from the build design: git -C work fetch origin prima/build, then git -C work show 8e96151dbe9ff03a55e6838168033ba6bf5f4a4a:<path> for docs/spec/examples/*.seq (11 files), docs/spec/WRITE-ONCE.md and docs/spec/Axioms.md. The hash-chain option may follow wf's own log (src/log.rs:2, each line holds the sha256 of the line before). Write-once fit is judged against Axioms.md:23 and docs/spec/WRITE-ONCE.md. Return: in noticed:, add a line starting "design review:" naming the design files you compared and what you found (t416u.md:7). Install wf once: cargo install --git https://github.com/Amalgamour/Workshop.git --rev c09fa60c92ac2e4cde39c73a061166ebc2fac0e0 --root D:\Git\codex\wf --locked wf (the binary is D:\Git\codex\wf\bin\wf.exe; same code as the returns branch today).
fields.stop if: you would change any file outside labs/0703/ (the return check refuses it); rusqlite will not build on your machine (end w01 need and say what failed; do not swap in another database silently); the timings are the only basis for the pick (say so); a rule above reads two ways. Do not commit target/ or the generated pages; the checks run cargo test, not the timing run, because timings differ by machine
fields.w01: new crate labs/0703/ (Cargo.toml with an empty [workspace] table, src/, a .gitignore holding target/). Generate about 1,000 sample pages from the shape of the 11 example .seq files, seeded so every run makes the same pages. Store them three ways: (a) one plain text file per page, committed with git; (b) one append-only log where each record holds the sha256 of the one before; (c) SQLite (the rusqlite crate with its bundled feature).
fields.w02: measure each store: time to write all pages, read all, read one; size on disk; hand-readability (can a person read one page in a plain editor, and why); tamper detection (change one byte: what finds it, and how); write-once fit (can a written page change without a trace). Unit tests: each store gives back the page it was given, and a one-byte change in the log is found.
fields.w03: labs/0703/LAB-0703-SEQ-STORAGE.md with sections "## 1. Options", "## 2. Sample pages", "## 3. Results" (a table, with the machine and OS the numbers came from), "## 4. Pick" (one option, with reasons tied to Axioms.md:23 and WRITE-ONCE.md, and what the others are still good for) and "## 5. How to rerun" (the exact commands).

# Return 90.50.10.0703.05.01
pack: 3cbdea445b7a6e063f446f4fad030b0f4f4821e39cb6f09f3f1419fb11578f92
done: Built a throwaway Rust trial of 1,000 seeded .seq pages in text with Git, an append-only SHA-256 log and bundled SQLite. Measured reads, writes, size and one-byte changes on Matthew's PC and documented the results and Codex's storage proposal.
changed: Created labs/0703/.gitignore, Cargo.lock, Cargo.toml, LAB-0703-SEQ-STORAGE.md, src/main.rs, src/sample.rs, src/store.rs, and .workshop/returns/90.50.10.0703.05.01.md.
noticed: SQLite's structural check passed after the body changed. The log needed a trusted head to detect an edit to its last record.
  design review: Compared docs/spec/examples/ (all 11 .seq files), docs/spec/Axioms.md:23 and docs/spec/WRITE-ONCE.md at 8e96151d, plus wf src/log.rs at c09fa60c. The examples set the face and event shapes. Axiom 6 and WRITE-ONCE support preserving earlier steps and keeping the delivery receipt with the change. The existing wf log shows the previous-record hash pattern.
w01: done - Standalone crate with ignored target/, deterministic corpus and three stores. The bundled SQLite build succeeded.
w02: done - Measured write-all, read-all, read-one and stored bytes. Ran a one-byte tamper trial for each and documented hand-readability and write-once fit.
w03: done - Report includes the measured machine and results, one Codex proposal with design citations, other uses and the exact rerun commands.
proof: This return is in the builder commit based on c09fa60c. cargo test --manifest-path labs/0703/Cargo.toml passed all six tests. git ls-files recognized the report and all three git grep heading checks passed. The locked release benchmark completed all seven rounds and the tamper trials.
not done: Claude's independent cross-check follows the return. Production durability, checkpoint custody and receipt replay are outside the trial.
unprompted: none
overflow: Codex proposal for a later trial: measure a rebuildable address-to-offset index backed by the verified log.
